paper_title: One-Sided-Error Parameterized Reductions for the Minimum Distance and Shortest Vector Problems
classifications: Theory of computation → Problems, reductions and completeness
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 5
statement: Our results leave several natural open questions. Can the assumption E ⊈ i.o.-NSIZE(2εn ) for some ε > 0 be removed from Theorems 4 and 5? For SVP, Theorem 2 gives randomized W[1]-hardness with one-sided error for γ < 21/p , whereas Bennett, Cheraghchi, Guruswami, and Ribeiro [7] obtained randomized hardness with two-sided error for every constant factor for fixed p > 1; can their entire approximation range be made one-sided error? For the Euclidean norm, Wan [40] proved √ deterministic polynomial-time NP-hardness of γ-GapSVP2 for every constant 1 ≤ γ < 2; √ can deterministic polynomial-time many-one hardness be extended to every constant γ ≥ 2?

For a positive integer N , we write [N ] := {1, . . . , N }. We write Z>0 for the set of positive integers. For a finite set S, its cardinality is denoted by |S|; for a string x, its bit length is denoted by |x|. We use ⟨x1 , . . . , xt ⟩ for a standard polynomial-time computable encoding of a tuple. Unless explicitly indicated otherwise, logarithms are base 2; logq denotes logarithm with base q. We use poly(·) for an unspecified polynomial and allow constants hidden in O(·) to depend on fixed constants such as p and q, and on γ whenever γ is fixed throughout the statement. We write Un for the uniform distribution over {0, 1}n .
